metadata.title: WonderFi Founder Says Canadian Crypto Rules Pushed Company Toward Robinhood

content.text:
WonderFi founder Karia Samaroo says Canada's capital markets and crypto regulatory structure made the company's C$250 million sale to Robinhood (NASDAQ: $HOOD) the clearest path to global scale, arguing that domestic success had become a ceiling rather than a launchpad.
Robinhood completed the acquisition on June 1, paying C$0.36 per WonderFi share, or roughly US$180 million in equity value. The deal gave Robinhood an established Canadian crypto operation and an investment dealer license, providing a regulated entry point into the market.
WonderFi brought about 300,000 funded customers, roughly US$800 million in crypto assets under custody and US$2.6 billion in trailing 12-month trading volume as of April. Its platforms include Bitbuy and Coinsquare, which are being migrated to Robinhood's Canadian crypto platform in phases.
More From Cryptoprowl:
Samaroo, who founded WonderFi in 2021, said the company had consolidated a fragmented domestic crypto market and survived both the FTX collapse and a sweeping regulatory overhaul. But scaling beyond Canada proved harder.
"Canada has created a ceiling for growth for ambitious companies," Samaroo wrote, pointing to thinner growth capital, weaker business investment, fragmented securities regulation and a less competitive environment for risk-taking.
Crypto firms face another layer of friction. Samaroo said Canada's post-Quadriga rules created one of the world's most demanding digital asset regimes, while provincial securities oversight added cost and complexity. He cited Binance, OKX, Bybit and Gemini (NASDAQ: $GEMI) among global exchanges that entered Canada before later exiting.
The sale gives Robinhood a shortcut into a market where building a compliant crypto platform from scratch carries a heavier regulatory burden. For WonderFi, it shifts the company from an independent Canadian consolidator into part of a larger U.S. financial platform with international ambitions.
Samaroo's argument leaves the deal carrying a broader question for Canada: whether successful fintechs can find enough capital and regulatory room to keep scaling independently once they outgrow the domestic market.
Robinhood Markets Inc. (NASDAQ: HOOD) stock is currently trading at $94.31 U.S. per share.
